title: toxicodendron zeyheri
intro: Toxicodendron zeyheri, commonly known as the Cape poison ivy or poison oak, is a plant species native to South Africa.  It is a member of the Anacardiaceae family and is known for its toxic sap that can cause skin irritation and allergic reactions in some individuals.  The plant has been used in traditional medicine to treat various health conditions, including fever, rheumatism, and skin conditions, with reported health benefits including anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties.  The bioactive constituents of Toxicodendron zeyheri include flavonoids, terpenoids, and alkaloids, which are believed to contribute to its therapeutic actions, including anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial activities.
